design: A/B/B/A changes only the RCCL process group high-priority stream option. All DDP groups are node-local with eight cards. Two checkpoint layers after the same prefix, no_sync on the first three microbatches, existing 25 MiB buckets and original Qwen LoRA geometry, clipping and AdamW in both arms. Form both process groups equally before measurement. Record actual options and synchronized update timings, first two optimizer states and peak GPU allocation.
rationale: The two completed 600-device component runs measured approximately 65 percent driver busy. Changing checkpoint spans or autocast caching gave diminishing compute-side gains. Check whether prioritizing RCCL gradient buckets changes the critical-path of a synchronized real update.
resource_policy: Retain the eight-card Qwen native node, sixteen unresolved MiniCPM cards, and sixteen previously identified external KFD cards. Former GLM pair nodes have original independent clean terminal checks. Gate all remaining nodes on current Slurm and worker PCI/KFD.
formal_qualification: Actual RCCL option and collectives in a generated-activation, same-shape training component. Physical HIP stream priority mapping and native Swift end-to-end speed are separate measurements.
original_grouped_behavior: Keep two-layer grouping and disabled autocast caching. Use the third in-scope experiment for a different communication variable and preserve the native training node.

optimizer.addressing: both arms use identical single foreach AdamW configuration; original scheduler behavior is not modeled
